links.outcome: Site-level alert reduction after AI activation
links.effect: Reduction varied by site: 33%, 24%, 17%, 39%; mean paired reductions 12.40, 2.55, -0.62, 0.26 alerts, none significant within site
links.quote: The magnitude of reduction varied between sites, suggesting heterogeneity in real-world implementation and warranting further evaluation of local workflow and programming factors (Table 1 ).

links.outcome: Clinician-facing alert burden and estimated physiologist review workload
links.effect: Clinician-facing alerts decreased from 4,261 to 2,509 (41.1%). Suppression of 1,007 alerts corresponded to estimated savings of 185-218 hours annually (3.6-4.2 hours per week); review time was not directly measured.
links.quote: Applying published time-and-motion estimates for remote transmission review (11-13 minutes per alert), suppression of 1,007 alerts by the AI algorithm was estimated to release approximately 185-218 hours of physiologist review time annually, equivalent to 3.6-4.2 hours per week of re-deployable service capacity.

links.outcome: Variation in operational alert suppression across sites
links.effect: Reported AI alert suppression was 33%, 24%, 17%, and 39% across four sites. Diagnostic accuracy and downstream clinical outcomes were not assessed.
links.quote: The magnitude of reduction varied between sites, suggesting heterogeneity in real-world implementation and warranting further evaluation of local workflow and programming factors (Table 1 ).
